tasks.short: Arrange orientation sessions, prepare materials, welcome new starters and record completion.

steps.what: Check new starters, start dates, locations and orientation requirements.
Find facilitator availability and book sessions.
Send joining instructions and confirm practical arrangements.
Assemble approved welcome materials for the starter group.
Welcome starters, explain expectations, answer questions and capture attendance.
Record attendance and completed orientation modules.
Copy completion status into the shared onboarding tracker.

tasks.design: Configure starter events from the {HCM} to create {CALENDAR} bookings and standard {EMAIL} instructions. A deterministic generator assembles approved {DOCS} materials, while an integration records attendance in the {LMS}; its completion view replaces the duplicate tracker. Facilitators keep the welcome conversation and handle unusual starter needs.
tasks.previous_blocker: Starter data, facilitator calendars and attendance records sat in separate places. Local variations made a single onboarding configuration awkward.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing scheduling and learning features handle much of the flow. AI-assisted coding reduces the effort of building the remaining connectors and template assembly.
tasks.still_hard: Facilitator availability, accessibility needs and late start-date changes still create exceptions. Attendance must be captured reliably.
tasks.human_edge: Notice uncertainty, explain unwritten expectations and help a starter feel comfortable asking questions.

ambition.what: First-month settling-in clinic for shift-based starters

tasks.altitude: The week contains fewer bookings and completion updates, with more time for starter questions and settling-in clinics. Booking exceptions can be delegated within agreed limits; policy and training requirements still need existing approval.

reach.learn: Learning objectives, accessible facilitation and completion evidence

reach.task: Resolve missing starter information before orientation
reach.learn: Record validation and onboarding exception handling

evidence.claim: Structured starter triggers, calendar bookings and completion records usually need configuration and deterministic integration.
GDPR applies to starter data; consultation requirements depend on national rules and the change introduced.
Dutch works council consent requirements cover specified HR data and monitoring arrangements.

assumptions: Time shares are illustrative estimates, informed by the supplied priors.
Orientation uses recurring sessions and approved materials.
The described baseline includes a duplicate onboarding tracker.
Standard invitations can be sent under approved scheduling rules.
Build ranges are working-day estimates for a limited pilot with available interfaces.
Consent and access includes employee consultation where national rules require it; formal proceedings may extend elapsed time.
unknowns: Which onboarding features are already configured
Available interfaces and calendar permissions
How attendance is captured
Starter volumes, locations and language needs
Applicable national consultation requirements
research_questions: Can existing configuration cover booking and invitations before custom code is needed?
Which orientation exceptions require a person to intervene?
Can completion views replace the tracker for every current user?
new_work: Resolve booking conflicts and late starter changes.
Maintain welcome templates and session rules.
Check failed attendance imports and incorrect completion records.
Keep access permissions and retention settings current.

tasks.short: Keep organisation charts, directories, handbooks and evaluation forms accurate and publish approved revisions.

steps.what: Collect document change requests and approved policy changes.
Export current employee, position and reporting-line records.
Update organisation charts and directories from current records.
Revise handbook wording and evaluation forms against approved changes.

loop.input: Current document, approved change instructions and approved policy sources
loop.output: Revised passages, source references and a revision comparison
loop.check: Validate references and protected fields; the specialist checks meaning before manager approval.
loop.stop: One draft and one correction pass per document; unresolved wording returns to manual editing.
loop.why_not_simpler: Policy wording arrives as prose and requires contextual edits. Fixed substitutions can change its meaning.

steps.what: Approve accuracy, policy meaning, effective dates and publication scope.
Publish approved versions and archive superseded documents.
Notify affected employees and managers of published changes.

tasks.design: Use configured views from the {HCM} for charts and directories, with structured change requests in the {WORKFLOW}. A bounded drafting loop edits prose in the {DOCS} from approved sources and produces a revision comparison. Recorded manager approval releases publication, archiving and targeted {EMAIL} notices.
tasks.previous_blocker: Personnel facts were copied into static documents, while policy changes arrived as prose. Version control and approval evidence were often disconnected.
tasks.enabler_now: Configured record views remove much copying. A bounded model loop can propose contextual edits, while deterministic checks preserve dates, references and approval requirements.
tasks.still_hard: Ambiguous policy changes, translations and inconsistent source records remain expensive. Evaluation forms require care because wording can affect employee assessment.
tasks.human_edge: Recognise when a wording change alters employee rights, manager discretion or the fairness of an evaluation.

ambition.what: Monthly selection of handbook passages needing clearer employee guidance

tasks.altitude: The week shifts from document copying to resolving source discrepancies and checking consequential edits. The specialist can prioritise clarity improvements within a delegated maintenance remit; policy approval remains with the HR manager.

reach.task: Improve employee and reporting-line record quality
reach.learn: Effective dating, validation rules and record ownership

reach.role: compensation, benefits and job analysis specialist
reach.task: Check job descriptions and evaluation criteria

evidence.claim: Charts and directories can be generated deterministically from authoritative personnel records.
Contextual prose revision can use bounded drafting with source checks and human approval.
Dutch national rules can require works council consent for HR data and monitoring arrangements.
The digest identifies gender-neutral job evaluation as relevant to pay transparency.

assumptions: Time shares are illustrative estimates, informed by the supplied priors.
Personnel records are authoritative for published organisation facts.
The existing systems can generate charts and directories; custom generation is a fallback.
Drafting changes wording only within approved policy instructions.
GDPR applies to personnel data; national rules govern additional consultation duties.
Build ranges cover a small document set and one language.
Consent and access includes required consultation; formal proceedings may extend elapsed time.
unknowns: Accuracy and effective dating of personnel records
Existing chart, directory and approval features
Number of document templates and languages
Who approves each document category
Publication audiences and confidentiality restrictions
Whether evaluation-form changes require employee consultation
research_questions: Which static documents can be replaced by governed live views?
Can protected clauses and effective dates be checked automatically?
How reliably can the draft retain meaning across the actual document set?
new_work: Review proposed wording and revision comparisons.
Maintain approved source documents and protected clauses.
Check publishing permissions, version history and failed notifications.
Recheck drafting quality when templates or model versions change.

tasks.short: Prepare policy options, discuss them with management and implement approved personnel procedures.

steps.what: Review personnel reports and recurring policy exceptions.
Select applicable policies and approved legal guidance.
Draft policy options, tradeoffs and an implementation proposal.

loop.input: Issue summary, selected policies, approved legal guidance and an options template
loop.output: Options brief with tradeoffs, source references and unanswered questions
loop.check: Check reference existence; the specialist verifies interpretation, omissions and practical consequences.
loop.stop: One draft and one correction pass; unsupported propositions stay flagged for manual review.
loop.why_not_simpler: Issues and policy sources are prose. Options require contextual synthesis that fixed templates cannot supply.

steps.what: Discuss options with managers and consult employee representatives where required.
Approve final policy wording, effective date and implementation responsibilities.
Issue implementation instructions and assign follow-up actions.

tasks.design: Configured {HCM} reports expose recurring exceptions, and a bounded loop drafts an options brief from selected {DOCS} sources. Managers and employee representatives keep the substantive discussion, with final approval recorded in the {WORKFLOW}. A deterministic flow turns the approved decision into assignments, document change requests and {EMAIL} instructions.
tasks.previous_blocker: The central work involves conflicting interests and context-dependent judgement. Preparation also required reading scattered policies and assembling bespoke briefs.
tasks.enabler_now: Governed sources and bounded drafting can shorten preparation. Small workflow tools can carry approved decisions into implementation without attempting to automate agreement.
tasks.still_hard: National employment rules, collective agreements and consultation processes vary. Trust, bargaining and the consequences of policy choices remain human work.
tasks.human_edge: Understand competing interests, test fairness and build an agreement managers and employees can accept.

ambition.what: Monthly review of recurring probation-policy exceptions

tasks.altitude: Most discussion and decision time remains. Faster preparation makes a monthly exception review practical; the specialist gains a clearer advisory remit, while formal policy authority stays with the authorised manager.

reach.task: Prepare employee consultation on proposed policy changes
reach.learn: National consultation procedures, collective agreements and negotiation preparation

reach.task: Assess the operational consequences of policy options
reach.learn: Option appraisal, implementation costs and measurable review criteria

evidence.claim: Policy preparation can use source-grounded drafting while discussion and approval remain human.
Dutch works council consent requirements apply to specified personnel arrangements.
A documented report failure illustrates why generated references require checking.

assumptions: Time shares are illustrative estimates, informed by the supplied priors.
The specialist supports management rather than holding final policy authority.
Approved legal guidance is supplied and maintained by qualified reviewers.
Required consultation occurs before final approval.
GDPR applies to personnel information; reporting should minimise identifiable data.
This solution drafts policy options and does not evaluate individual workers.
Build ranges cover one policy workflow; consultation may extend elapsed time.
unknowns: Applicable countries, collective agreements and national procedures
Existing approval and employee consultation arrangements
Availability of approved legal guidance
Quality of policy exception records
Who can authorise policy pilots and final changes
research_questions: Which exception patterns can be reported without identifying employees?
What sources must every options brief include?
Which implementation actions can follow a recorded approval automatically?
new_work: Verify draft interpretations and source references.
Record consultation outcomes and unresolved objections.
Monitor implementation actions and overdue reviews.
Define useful exception categories without introducing employee profiling.

tasks.short: Tell applicants their application status, explain decisions and record the communication.

steps.what: Check application stage, recorded decisions and outstanding communication.
Ask hiring managers to resolve missing or stale status information.
Prepare a status message or call brief from the application record.
Check final notices and add appropriate personalised feedback.
Send written updates to the correct applicants.
Call applicants when decisions or questions need a personal explanation.
Log messages, conversation notes and required follow-up.

tasks.design: Configure {ATS} stage triggers, approved templates and reminders for missing hiring-manager updates. Routine progress messages send automatically through {EMAIL}; final decision notices require recorded recruiter approval, and delivery results return to the {ATS}. Recruiters keep personal calls and enter concise conversation notes.
tasks.previous_blocker: Application stages and decisions were not always current. Templates existed, but recruiters still chased managers, checked recipients and copied communication records.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing recruitment messaging and trigger features cover the core flow. Small integrations can close delivery and logging gaps without a model or autonomous agent.
tasks.still_hard: Automation cannot communicate an unrecorded decision accurately. Personal feedback, disputed outcomes and applicant questions need judgement and care.
tasks.human_edge: Explain disappointing outcomes respectfully, answer concerns and distinguish useful feedback from unsupported assertions.

ambition.what: Applicants requesting accessible status updates in their preferred contact format

tasks.altitude: The week contains fewer routine sends and manager reminders, with more time for difficult calls and overdue decisions. The recruiter can choose contact format and escalate delays within agreed rules; selection authority does not change.

reach.task: Monitor failed applicant notices and missing contact details
reach.learn: Delivery troubleshooting, identity checks and retention rules

reach.task: Review accessibility and fairness of applicant communications
reach.learn: Accessible formats, consistent explanations and complaint handling

evidence.claim: Recruitment stage triggers and approved templates can automate routine status communication without a model.
GDPR Article 22 restricts solely automated decisions with legal or similarly significant effects.
A determining automated score can fall within the automated-decision rules.

assumptions: Time shares are illustrative estimates; the supplied mail share is treated as a weak prior.
This workflow communicates recorded selection decisions and does not make or score them.
Routine progress updates use approved wording and current application stages.
Final decision notices send only after recorded recruiter approval.
The existing recruitment system supports triggers, templates and communication logging.
Contact preferences are supplied voluntarily without inferring disability or other sensitive attributes.
GDPR applies; employee consultation requirements depend on national rules and the proposed change.
Build ranges cover one recruitment pipeline and include access and required consultation.
unknowns: Reliability of application stages and recorded decisions
Existing messaging, approval and logging features
Who may approve final decision communications
Volume of personal calls and disputed outcomes
Applicant contact preferences and accessible formats
Retention settings and applicable national consultation requirements
research_questions: Which existing features can remove manual sending and logging?
Can final notices be technically blocked without recorded approval?
What happens when a decision changes after a message is queued?
Which applicant questions require a personal call?
new_work: Handle bounced messages and incorrect contact details.
Maintain templates, triggers and approval permissions.
Review queued notices after decision changes.
Resolve missing status updates and overdue manager responses.
Enter concise call notes and manage applicant follow-up.

role.altitude: The HR specialist spends less time copying records, booking sessions and sending routine notices. More of the week goes to starter support, careful policy preparation and consequential communications; additional authority requires explicit delegation.
reach: Support training and development specialists with first-month learning pathways.
Help HR assistants improve source records and handle workflow exceptions.
Prepare better consultation material for labor relations specialists.
Work with equal opportunity representatives on accessible applicant communications.
skills_to_grow: Configure event triggers, templates and approval rules.
Validate personnel records and effective dates.
Check generated prose against approved sources.
Understand GDPR and applicable national consultation rules.
Facilitate difficult conversations and assess policy tradeoffs.
Measure delays, exceptions and service quality.
role.ambitious_version: Provide a structured first-month support service and a monthly policy-exception review, alongside accessible applicant updates. Use governed records and deterministic workflows for preparation and follow-through, with people retaining consequential judgements.
